newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on 90-day storage, CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on 90-day storage, CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on a heavy selloff of 90-day storage certificates and lower CBOT soycomplex values, traders said.

"About 1,000 90-day tickets were sold in the March, there was good exporter scale down buying, 900 to 1,000 Jan-March spread," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $2, then $1.80 and $2.30. January futures crush margin rose to -36.19 from -36.93 Thursday. Volume was 5,440 lots, or 108,800 tonnes.
Japan bought 8,000-10,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
January canola fell $3 to $402. January flax fell $1.50 to $357 on 90-day tickets. Mar-May spread at $3, Jan-Mar $4.
March feed wheat fell $2.50 to $168.90 on commercial sales to realign spreads. Mar-May $1, Mar-July $2. Volume 855 lots.
February western barley fell $1.20 at $136.50, March lost $1.10 to $136.10 on commerical and Midland Walwyn sales, traders said. Volume was 1,200 lots.
UGG bought December peas unchanged at US$185 from Cargill, traders said. Oct-Dec spread at US$1. Volume was 15 lots.
Commercials bought May oats unchanged at US$116, October oats up US$2.50 at US$116.50 and December up US$2.50 to US$117 from commission houses. Volume was 70 lots.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats).
